name: Indie Hacker Tools

sources.title: The repo of tools made by indie hackers
Founder post: listing is completely free and always will be

requirements: Tools must be made by indie hackers (apps, books, courses, newsletters, etc.)
First-time submitters create a maker profile; returning submitters skip that step
Listing is explicitly free per the founder and the site ('List your tool for free')
preparation: Tool name, URL, short description, and logo (per third-party guides)
Maker/indie-hacker identity details for the profile step (first-time listers)
Pick the right badge/status: listings show states like 'Launched', 'Generating revenue', 'Work in progress'
workflow: Choose 'It's my first time listing a tool' (goes to /list-tool, includes profile creation) or 'I have listed a tool before' (goes to /list)
Fill the tool listing form and submit for review
watchFor: The form pages (/list-tool, /list) are JS-rendered and did not expose fields to a plain fetch - inspect in a browser before automating
The catalog's canonical /submit URL 404s; the real entry point is /list-indie-tool
Site is a small indie project - review turnaround is unknown
countsAsLive: The tool appears as a card on indiehacker.tools homepage/browse with a status badge and outbound link.
unknowns: Exact form fields and whether an account system or magic-link email is used
Whether outbound links are dofollow (third-party sources disagree: backlinkbot says dofollow, catalog DR differs)
